brief: Posts today centered on the Riemann Hypothesis breakthrough and how builders work with models, alongside the GTA VI launch and a ChatGPT/Codex desktop update. The most notable item beyond that was Thibault Sottiaux asking users what still needs attention after the Codex desktop app update.

themes.label: Riemann Hypothesis AI breakthrough
themes.summary: Builders debated how seriously to take AI's role in the Riemann Hypothesis result, with Aaron Levie calling it an era-changing shift and Matt Turck noting the hype outran understanding.

themes.label: GTA VI and AI-built PC ports
themes.summary: Builders connected the GTA VI debate to AI, with Amjad Masad citing a student recompiling the game for PC and Garry Tan floating a vibe-coded PC port.

themes.label: ChatGPT and Codex desktop updates
themes.summary: Builders reacted to the new ChatGPT mobile app and the Codex desktop update, with Thibault Sottiaux asking for feedback on remaining gaps and Peter Yang suggesting UI fixes.

builders.name: Amjad Masad
builders.summary: Highlighted a high school student recompiling GTA VI for PC using GitHub issues to coordinate agent swarms. He also announced that Amuse, built by Replit Missions, is open source.

builders.name: Thariq
builders.summary: Argued that working with models is a deep technical skill that grows in importance as models improve. He also warned against disintermediating ourselves too quickly.

builders.name: Peter Yang
builders.summary: Shared a tip for pinning Codex to the ChatGPT mobile bottom nav and suggested adding local Codex threads to the left nav. He also commented on GTA VI complaints.

builders.name: Thibault Sottiaux
builders.summary: Said the team is preparing another big update and asked users what still needs attention after the ChatGPT/Codex desktop update. His other post was a brief remark about checking out threads.

builders.name: Matt Turck
builders.summary: Recapped the first Slush conference, praising its organization and format. He also joked about the Riemann Hypothesis hype and posted a personal remark.

builders.name: Aaron Levie
builders.summary: Shared a post arguing the Riemann Hypothesis breakthrough matters beyond math because problem-solving is changing. He said no current AI alone can do this work.

builders.name: Dan Shipper
builders.summary: Recommended a piece on benchmarks, noting that the numbers may not mean what they seem to. He also joked about bad technology takes.

builders.name: Guillermo Rauch
builders.summary: Posted a brief call for a tool for AI feats, with little context. His only post was one line.

builders.name: Garry Tan
builders.summary: Said he uses the tool for about half his work with his software factory and calls it the best experience so far. He also suggested a vibe-coded GTA VI PC port could come soon.

builders.name: Swyx
builders.summary: Questioned why AI providers were secretly phoning home, calling it alarming. His post was a single question.

builders.name: Zara Zhang
builders.summary: Posted a short message: Build for yourself. Nothing more substantive today.

builders.name: No Priors
builders.summary: Published a podcast episode with Max Jaderberg, President of Isomorphic Labs, on AI-driven drug discovery and predicting toxicity before patient trials.

builders.name: Nan Yu
builders.summary: Posted a short quip, Forget second brain. Third brain. All personal or minor posts today.
